NKJV.1: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had stayed two days in Ziklag,
NKJV.2: on the third day, behold, it happened that a man came from Saul’s camp with his clothes torn and dust on his head. So it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the ground and prostrated himself.
NKJV.3: And David said to him, “Where have you come from?” So he said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Israel.”
NKJV.4: Then David said to him, “How did the matter go? Please tell me.” And he answered, “The people have fled from the battle, many of the people are fallen and dead, and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.”
NKJV.5: So David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?”
NKJV.6: Then the young man who told him said, “As I happened by chance to be on Mount Gilboa, there was Saul, leaning on his spear; and indeed the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
NKJV.7: Now when he looked behind him, he saw me and called to me. And I answered, ‘Here I am.’
NKJV.8: And he said to me, ‘Who are you?’ So I answered him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
NKJV.9: He said to me again, ‘Please stand over me and kill me, for anguish has come upon me, but my life still remains in me.’
NKJV.10: So I stood over him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.”
NKJV.11: Therefore David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.
NKJV.12: And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son, for the people of the LORD and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
NKJV.13: Then David said to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?” And he answered, “I am the son of an alien, an Amalekite.”
NKJV.14: So David said to him, “How was it you were not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
NKJV.15: Then David called one of the young men and said, “Go near, and execute him!” And he struck him so that he died.
NKJV.16: So David said to him, “Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have killed the LORD’s anointed.’ ”
NKJV.17: Then David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
NKJV.18: and he told them to teach the children of Judah the Song of the Bow; indeed it is written in the Book of Jasher:
NKJV.19: “The beauty of Israel is slain on your high places!  How the mighty have fallen!
NKJV.20: Tell it not in Gath, Proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon— Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
NKJV.21: “O mountains of Gilboa, Let there be no dew nor rain upon you, Nor fields of offerings. For the shield of the mighty is cast away there! The shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
NKJV.22: From the blood of the slain, From the fat of the mighty,  The bow of Jonathan did not turn back, And the sword of Saul did not return empty.
NKJV.23: “Saul and Jonathan were beloved and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they were not divided; They were swifter than eagles, They were stronger than lions.
NKJV.24: “O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, Who clothed you in scarlet, with luxury; Who put ornaments of gold on your apparel.
NKJV.25: “How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan was slain in your high places.
NKJV.26: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan; You have been very pleasant to me;  Your love to me was wonderful, Surpassing the love of women.
NKJV.27: “How  the mighty have fallen, And the weapons of war perished!”

NASB.1: Now it came about after the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, that David remained two days in Ziklag.
NASB.2: On the third day, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes torn and dust on his head. And it came about when he came to David that he fell to the ground and prostrated himself.
NASB.3: Then David said to him, 'From where do you come?' And he said to him, 'I have escaped from the camp of Israel.'
NASB.4: David said to him, 'How did things go? Please tell me.' And he said, 'The people have fled from the battle, and also many of the people have fallen and are dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.'
NASB.5: So David said to the young man who told him, 'How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?'
NASB.6: The young man who told him said, 'By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and behold, Saul was leaning on his spear. And behold, the chariots and the horsemen pursued him closely.
NASB.7: 'When he looked behind him, he saw me and called to me. And I said, 'Here I am.'
NASB.8: 'He said to me, 'Who are you?' And I answered him, 'I am an Amalekite.'
NASB.9: 'Then he said to me, 'Please stand beside me and kill me, for agony has seized me because my life still lingers in me.'
NASB.10: 'So I stood beside him and killed him, because I knew that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown which [was] on his head and the bracelet which [was] on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.'
NASB.11: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and [so] also [did] all the men who [were] with him.
NASB.12: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
NASB.13: David said to the young man who told him, 'Where are you from?' And he answered, 'I am the son of an alien, an Amalekite.'
NASB.14: Then David said to him, 'How is it you were not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed?'
NASB.15: And David called one of the young men and said, 'Go, cut him down.' So he struck him and he died.
NASB.16: David said to him, 'Your blood is on your head, for your mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I have killed the LORD'S anointed.''
NASB.17: Then David chanted with this lament over Saul and Jonathan his son,
NASB.18: and he told [them] to teach the sons of Judah [the song of] the bow; behold, it is written in the book of Jashar.
NASB.19: 'Your beauty, O Israel, is slain on your high places! How have the mighty fallen!
NASB.20: 'Tell [it] not in Gath, Proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, Or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice, The daughters of the uncircumcised will exult.
NASB.21: 'O mountains of Gilboa, Let not dew or rain be on you, nor fields of offerings; For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, The shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
NASB.22: 'From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, The bow of Jonathan did not turn back, And the sword of Saul did not return empty.
NASB.23: 'Saul and Jonathan, beloved and pleasant in their life, And in their death they were not parted; They were swifter than eagles, They were stronger than lions.
NASB.24: 'O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, Who clothed you luxuriously in scarlet, Who put ornaments of gold on your apparel.
NASB.25: 'How have the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is slain on your high places.
NASB.26: 'I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan; You have been very pleasant to me. Your love to me was more wonderful Than the love of women.
NASB.27: 'How have the mighty fallen, And the weapons of war perished!'

ESV.1: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from striking down the Amalekites, David remained two days in Ziklag.
ESV.2: And on the third day, behold, a man came from Saul's camp, with his clothes torn and dirt on his head. And when he came to David, he fell to the ground and paid homage.
ESV.3: David said to him, “Where do you come from?” And he said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Israel.”
ESV.4: And David said to him, “How did it go? Tell me.” And he answered, “The people fled from the battle, and also many of the people have fallen and are dead, and Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”
ESV.5: Then David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”
ESV.6: And the young man who told him said, “By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear, and behold, the chariots and the horsemen were close upon him.
ESV.7: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, ‘Here I am.’
ESV.8: And he said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I answered him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
ESV.9: And he said to me, ‘Stand beside me and kill me, for anguish has seized me, and yet my life still lingers.’
ESV.10: So I stood beside him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”
ESV.11: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men who were with him.
ESV.12: And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for the people of the LORD and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
ESV.13: And David said to the young man who told him, “Where do you come from?” And he answered, “I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite.”
ESV.14: David said to him, “How is it you were not afraid to put out your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?”
ESV.15: Then David called one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him.” And he struck him down so that he died.
ESV.16: And David said to him, “Your blood be on your head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have killed the LORD's anointed.’”
ESV.17: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and Jonathan his son,
ESV.18: and he said it  should be taught to the people of Judah; behold, it is written in the Book of Jashar.  He said:
ESV.19: “Your glory, O Israel, is slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen!
ESV.20: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
ESV.21: “You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain upon you, nor fields of offerings!  For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
ESV.22: “From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.
ESV.23: “Saul and Jonathan, beloved and lovely! In life and in death they were not divided; they were swifter than eagles; they were stronger than lions.
ESV.24: “You daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you luxuriously in scarlet, who put ornaments of gold on your apparel.
ESV.25: “How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle!  “Jonathan lies slain on your high places.
ESV.26: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan; very pleasant have you been to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.
ESV.27: “How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war perished!”

AMP.1: Now it happened after the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, that he stayed two days in Ziklag.
AMP.2: On the third day a man came [unexpectedly] from Saul's camp with his clothes torn and dust on his head [as in mourning]. When he came to David, he bowed to the ground and lay himself face down [in an act of great respect and submission].
AMP.3: Then David asked him, "Where do you come from?" He said, "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
AMP.4: David said to him, "How did it go? Please tell me." He answered, "The people have fled from the battle. Also, many of the people have fallen and are dead; Saul and Jonathan his son are also dead."
AMP.5: So David said to the young man who informed him, "How do you know Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"
AMP.6: And the young man who told him explained, "By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear, and the chariots and horsemen [of the Philistines] were close behind him.
AMP.7: When he turned to look behind him, he saw me, and called to me. And I answered, 'Here I am.'
AMP.8: He asked me, 'Who are you?' I answered him, 'I am an Amalekite.'
AMP.9: He said to me, 'Stand up facing me and kill me, for [terrible] agony has come over me, yet I still live [and I will be taken alive].'
AMP.10: So I stood facing him and killed him, because I knew that he could not live after he had fallen. Then I took the crown which was on his head and the band which was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord."
AMP.11: Then David grasped his own clothes and tore them [in mourning]; so did all the men who were with him.
AMP.12: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and Jonathan his son, and for the Lord's people and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword [in battle].
AMP.13: David said to the young man who informed him, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am the son of a foreigner (resident alien, sojourner), an Amalekite."
AMP.14: David said to him, "How is it that you were not afraid to put out your hand to destroy the <e>Lord's</e> anointed?"
AMP.15: David called one of the young men and said, "Go, execute him." So he struck the Amalekite and he died.
AMP.16: David said to the [fallen] man, " Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying, 'I have killed the Lord's anointed.'"
AMP.17: Then David sang this dirge (funeral song) over Saul and his son Jonathan,
AMP.18: and he told them to teach the sons of Judah, the song of the bow. Behold, it is written in the Book of Jashar:
AMP.19:
"Your glory and splendor, O Israel, is slain upon your high places!
How the mighty have fallen!
AMP.20:
"Tell it not in Gath,
Proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon,
Or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice,
The daughters of the uncircumcised (pagans) will exult.
AMP.21:
" O mountains of Gilboa,
Let not dew or rain be upon you, nor fields with offerings;
For there the shield of the mighty was defiled,
The shield of Saul, [dry, cracked] not anointed with oil.
AMP.22:
"From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty,
The bow of Jonathan did not turn back,
And the sword of Saul did not return empty.
AMP.23:
"Saul and Jonathan, beloved and lovely and friends in their lives,
And in their death they were not separated;
They were swifter than eagles,
They were stronger than lions.
AMP.24:
"O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul,
Who clothed you luxuriously in scarlet,
Who put ornaments of gold on your apparel.
AMP.25:
"How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle!
Jonathan lies slain upon your high places.
AMP.26:
"I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan;
You have been a good friend to me.
Your love toward me was more wonderful
Than the love of women.
AMP.27:
"How the mighty have fallen,
And the weapons of war have perished!"

CSB17.3: David asked him, “Where have you come from?” He replied to him, “I’ve escaped from the Israelite camp.”
CSB17.4: “What was the outcome? Tell me,” David asked him. “The troops fled from the battle,” he answered. “Many of the troops have fallen and are dead. Also, Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.” <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.5: David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”

NLT.1: After the death of Saul, David returned from his victory over the Amalekites and spent two days in Ziklag.
NLT.2: On the third day a man arrived from Saul’s army camp. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show that he was in mourning. He fell to the ground before David in deep respect.
NLT.3: “Where have you come from?” David asked. “I escaped from the Israelite camp,” the man replied.
NLT.4: “What happened?” David demanded. “Tell me how the battle went.” The man replied, “Our entire army fled from the battle. Many of the men are dead, and Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”
NLT.5: “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?” David demanded of the young man.
NLT.6: The man answered, “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear with the enemy chariots and charioteers closing in on him.
NLT.7: When he turned and saw me, he cried out for me to come to him. ‘How can I help?’ I asked him.
NLT.8: “He responded, ‘Who are you?’ “‘I am an Amalekite,’ I told him.
NLT.9: “Then he begged me, ‘Come over here and put me out of my misery, for I am in terrible pain and want to die.’
NLT.10: “So I killed him,” the Amalekite told David, “for I knew he couldn’t live. Then I took his crown and his armband, and I have brought them here to you, my lord.”
NLT.11: David and his men tore their clothes in sorrow when they heard the news.
NLT.12: They mourned and wept and fasted all day for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the LORD’s army and the nation of Israel, because they had died by the sword that day.
NLT.13: Then David said to the young man who had brought the news, “Where are you from?” And he replied, “I am a foreigner, an Amalekite, who lives in your land.”
NLT.14: “Why were you not afraid to kill the LORD’s anointed one?” David asked.
NLT.15: Then David said to one of his men, “Kill him!” So the man thrust his sword into the Amalekite and killed him.
NLT.16: “You have condemned yourself,” David said, “for you yourself confessed that you killed the LORD’s anointed one.”
NLT.17: Then David composed a funeral song for Saul and Jonathan,
NLT.18: and he commanded that it be taught to the people of Judah. It is known as the Song of the Bow, and it is recorded in The Book of Jashar.
NLT.19:
Your pride and joy, O Israel, lies dead on the hills!
Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen!
NLT.20:
Don’t announce the news in Gath,
don’t proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon,
or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice
and the pagans will laugh in triumph.
NLT.21:
O mountains of Gilboa,
let there be no dew or rain upon you,
nor fruitful fields producing offerings of grain.
For there the shield of the mighty heroes was defiled;
the shield of Saul will no longer be anointed with oil.
NLT.22:
The bow of Jonathan was powerful,
and the sword of Saul did its mighty work.
They shed the blood of their enemies
and pierced the bodies of mighty heroes.
NLT.23:
How beloved and gracious were Saul and Jonathan!
They were together in life and in death.
They were swifter than eagles,
stronger than lions.
NLT.24:
O women of Israel, weep for Saul,
for he dressed you in luxurious scarlet clothing,
in garments decorated with gold.
NLT.25:
Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen in battle!
Jonathan lies dead on the hills.
NLT.26:
How I weep for you, my brother Jonathan!
Oh, how much I loved you!
And your love for me was deep,
deeper than the love of women!
NLT.27:
Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen!
Stripped of their weapons, they lie dead.

MSG.1: Shortly after Saul died, David returned to Ziklag from his rout of the Amalekites.
MSG.2:
Three days later a man showed up unannounced from Saul's army camp.
Disheveled and obviously in mourning, he fell to his knees in respect before David.
MSG.3:
David asked, "What brings you here?"
He answered, "I've just escaped from the camp of Israel."
MSG.4:
"So what happened?" said David. "What's the news?"
He said, "The Israelites have fled the battlefield, leaving a lot of their dead comrades behind. And Saul and his son Jonathan are dead."
MSG.5: David pressed the young soldier for details: "How do you know for sure that Saul and Jonathan are dead?"
MSG.6: "I just happened by Mount Gilboa and came on Saul, badly wounded and leaning on his spear, with enemy chariots and horsemen bearing down hard on him.
MSG.7: He looked behind him, saw me, and called me to him. 'Yes sir,' I said, 'at your service.'
MSG.8: He asked me who I was, and I told him, 'I'm an Amalekite.' "
MSG.9: "Come here," he said, "and put me out of my misery. I'm nearly dead already, but my life hangs on."
MSG.10: "So I did what he asked—I killed him. I knew he wouldn't last much longer anyway. I removed his royal headband and bracelet, and have brought them to my master. Here they are."
MSG.11: In lament, David ripped his clothes to ribbons. All the men with him did the same.
MSG.12: They wept and fasted the rest of the day, grieving the death of Saul and his son Jonathan, and also the army of God and the nation Israel, victims in a failed battle.
MSG.13:
Then David spoke to the young soldier who had brought the report: "Who are you, anyway?"
"I'm from an immigrant family—an Amalekite."
MSG.14: "Do you mean to say," said David, "that you weren't afraid to up and kill God's anointed king?"
MSG.15: Right then he ordered one of his soldiers, "Strike him dead!" The soldier struck him, and he died.
MSG.16: "You asked for it," David told him. "You sealed your death sentence when you said you killed God's anointed king."
MSG.17: Then David sang this lament over Saul and his son Jonathan,
MSG.18: and gave orders that everyone in Judah learn it by heart. Yes, it's even inscribed in The Book of Jashar.
MSG.19:
Oh, oh, Gazelles of Israel, struck down on your hills,
the mighty warriors—fallen, fallen!
MSG.20:
Don't announce it in the city of Gath,
don't post the news in the streets of Ashkelon.
Don't give those coarse Philistine girls
one more excuse for a drunken party!
MSG.21:
No more dew or rain for you, hills of Gilboa,
and not a drop from springs and wells,
For there the warriors' shields were dragged through the mud,
Saul's shield left there to rot.
MSG.22:
Jonathan's bow was bold—
the bigger they were the harder they fell.
Saul's sword was fearless—
once out of the scabbard, nothing could stop it.
MSG.23:
Saul and Jonathan—beloved, beautiful!
Together in life, together in death.
Swifter than plummeting eagles,
stronger than proud lions.
MSG.24:
Women of Israel, weep for Saul.
He dressed you in finest cottons and silks,
spared no expense in making you elegant.
MSG.25:
The mighty warriors—fallen, fallen
in the middle of the fight!
Jonathan—struck down on your hills!
MSG.26:
O my dear brother Jonathan,
I'm crushed by your death.
Your friendship was a miracle-wonder,
love far exceeding anything I've known—
or ever hope to know.
MSG.27:
The mighty warriors—fallen, fallen.
And the arms of war broken to bits.

NET.1: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from defeating the Amalekites, he stayed at Ziklag for two days.
NET.2: On the third day a man arrived from the camp of Saul with his clothes torn and dirt on his head. When he approached David, the man threw himself to the ground.
NET.3: David asked him, “Where are you coming from?” He replied, “I have escaped from the camp of Israel.”
NET.4: David inquired, “How were things going? Tell me!” He replied, “The people fled from the battle and many of them fell dead. Even Saul and his son Jonathan are dead!”
NET.5: David said to the young man who was telling him this, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”
NET.6: The young man who was telling him this said, “I just happened to be on Mount Gilboa and came across Saul leaning on his spear for support. The chariots and leaders of the horsemen were in hot pursuit of him.
NET.7: When he turned around and saw me, he called out to me. I answered, ‘Here I am!’
NET.8: He asked me, ‘Who are you?’ I told him, ‘I’m an Amalekite.’
NET.9: He said to me, ‘Stand over me and finish me off! I’m very dizzy, even though I’m still alive.’
NET.10: So I stood over him and put him to death, since I knew that he couldn’t live in such a condition. Then I took the crown which was on his head and the bracelet which was on his arm. I have brought them here to my lord.”
NET.11: David then grabbed his own clothes and tore them, as did all the men who were with him.
NET.12: They lamented and wept and fasted until evening because Saul, his son Jonathan, the LORD’s people, and the house of Israel had fallen by the sword.
NET.13: David said to the young man who told this to him, “Where are you from?” He replied, “I am an Amalekite, the son of a resident foreigner.”
NET.14: David replied to him, “How is it that you were not afraid to reach out your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”
NET.15: Then David called one of the soldiers and said, “Come here and strike him down!” So he struck him down, and he died.
NET.16: David said to him, “Your blood be on your own head! Your own mouth has testified against you, saying ‘I have put the LORD’s anointed to death.’”
NET.17: Then David chanted this lament over Saul and his son Jonathan.
NET.18: (He gave instructions that the people of Judah should be taught “The Bow.” Indeed, it is written down in the Book of Yashar.)
NET.19: The beauty of Israel lies slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen!
NET.20: Don’t report it in Gath, don’t spread the news in the streets of Ashkelon, or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice, the daughters of the uncircumcised will celebrate!
NET.21: O mountains of Gilboa, may there be no dew or rain on you, nor fields of grain offerings! For it was there that the shield of warriors was defiled; the shield of Saul lies neglected without oil.
NET.22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of warriors, the bow of Jonathan was not turned away. The sword of Saul never returned empty.
NET.23: Saul and Jonathan were greatly loved during their lives, and not even in their deaths were they separated. They were swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.
NET.24: O daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet as well as jewelry, who put gold jewelry on your clothes.
NET.25: How the warriors have fallen in the midst of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your high places!
NET.26: I grieve over you, my brother Jonathan! You were very dear to me. Your love was more special to me than the love of women.
NET.27: How the warriors have fallen! The weapons of war are destroyed!
